research: https://cloud.google.com/blog/products/ai-machine-learning/ultimate-prompting-guide-for-nano-banana — Google's own guide: write a narrative sentence, not a keyword list; order Subject + Action + Location + Composition + Style; use real camera language (shot size, angle, 'shallow depth of field (f/1.8)'); name specific materials; describe what you want rather than what you don't (negatives backfire); 9:16 is a native ratio; give each attached reference an explicit role

https://dev.to/googleai/getting-the-most-out-of-nano-banana-2-502k — Google AI on Nano Banana 2: say 'photorealistic' outright, name the light source and its quality, mimic a capture device via lens/sensor traits (e.g. high-ISO noise); anchor to a reference with 'based on the attached reference' when one is used

https://www.studiobinder.com/blog/low-light-photography-settings/ and https://greatbigphotographyworld.com/night-street-photography/ — night bokeh comes from fast primes wide open (f/1.4-f/1.8) with lights far behind the subject; distant lights become big soft circles, near ones stay pinpoints

https://alphauniverse.com/stories/how-to-create-magic-portraits and https://expertphotography.com/night-portrait-photography — 85-135mm telephoto compression pulls the bokeh circles up close behind the subject so the frame reads as 'night city'; let shop windows, neon and street lamps be the key light and turn the face toward one

https://www.podcastvideos.com/articles/cinematography-tips-shooting-night-exteriors/ and https://artlist.io/blog/night-scene-videography/ — night exteriors are lit by practicals (warm street lamp as key, a touch of cool fill), spill controlled so the blacks stay inky; a wet pavement adds reflections that multiply the bokeh
attach_reference: yes, as a style-only reference — the photo IS the look (its exact bokeh size, amber/red/cyan mix, glowing roof-sign colour and crushed blacks are hard to hit by words alone), but say in the prompt 'use the attached photo only for its colour, light and lens look' so Nano Banana does not copy its composition or turn the shot into two car roofs with no lad; the prompts below also describe the look fully, so they still work unattached.
notes: The line 'One version of me gets home fine.' is voice/subtitle in the edit, never in the image. If the TAXI sign comes back misspelt or with extra words, re-roll rather than edit; prompt 3 keeps the sign partly out of frame to reduce that risk. Leave headroom/footroom in 9:16 for platform captions. The lad's description is identical in all three prompts so any pick can feed the split-screen beat B.

prompts.idea: Low-angle hero close-up on an 85mm wide open: keys thrust at the lens, cocky grin, pub glow and taxis melting behind him. Stops the scroll because he is pointing at YOU.
prompts.prompt: Photorealistic vertical 9:16 night film still. A young man in his early twenties with short dark hair and an untucked white going-out shirt, flushed and a little sweaty, stands outside a British pub at closing time, mid-sentence, grinning with drunk certainty as he thrusts a lanyard of car keys up toward the camera. Low-angle medium close-up on an 85mm lens at f/1.4: his face is razor sharp, the dangling keys catch a glint, and the street behind him dissolves into huge soft bokeh circles of warm amber, red, a little pink and cyan, with two glowing yellow taxi roof signs blurred in the distance. The only light is the pub window's warm spill on his cheek and a street lamp's rim on his hair; deep inky blacks, fine film grain. Thanks.

prompts.idea: Long telephoto from across the road, framed over a soft taxi roof exactly like the reference: the waiting cab he should take sits in the foreground while he waves the keys at it. The irony is in the frame.
prompts.prompt: Photorealistic vertical 9:16 night film still, shot on a 135mm telephoto at f/1.8 from across a wet city street. In the soft out-of-focus foreground, the bottom third of the frame is the silver roof of a parked car with a glowing yellow roof sign reading "TAXI", its light reflected on the paintwork. Beyond it, sharp, a young man in his early twenties with short dark hair and an untucked white going-out shirt, flushed and a little sweaty, stands on the pavement outside a pub, holding his lanyard of car keys high and talking with smug drunk confidence. Behind him, shop windows and street lamps melt into large creamy bokeh discs of amber, red, pink and cyan. Inky blacks, practical light only, cinematic grain. Thanks.

prompts.idea: Tight side-on profile, 50mm, the taxi sign as his key light: he leans toward a cab window jangling the keys, face washed in yellow sign-glow, the rest of the night blown to bokeh. Intimate and funny, and it sets up the taxi payoff.
prompts.prompt: Photorealistic vertical 9:16 night film still. Tight three-quarter profile close-up on a 50mm lens at f/1.2 of a young man in his early twenties with short dark hair and an untucked white going-out shirt, flushed and a little sweaty, leaning toward the kerb outside a pub and lifting a lanyard of car keys beside his face, mouth open mid-boast, eyebrows raised in total drunk certainty. His face is lit by the warm yellow glow of a taxi roof sign just out of frame at the edge, a hard golden key light with deep shadow on the far cheek. Everything behind him is a dark street turned into big soft bokeh circles of amber, red, pink and a cool cyan, reflected in the wet pavement. Inky blacks, shallow focus, subtle grain. Thanks.
